issues.legal_issue: A tenant of agricultural land who remains in possession after a fixed-term lease expires does not thereby become a trespasser and may be evicted only through the applicable agricultural-tenancy process.
material_facts: The landlord’s case was that the agricultural land had been leased to the tenant for fixed terms and that the last lease expired in 2005.
The landlord acknowledged that the tenant had been in possession from 1986 through 2005, and revenue records recorded the tenant’s possession.
The tenant remained in possession after the lease expired and claimed protection under the agricultural-tenancy laws.
The landlord sought possession through a civil-court counterclaim; no eviction through the designated revenue process was shown.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the lower courts erred in treating the agricultural tenant as a trespasser merely because the fixed-term lease had expired. In the Court’s view, eviction had to proceed under the applicable tenancy law before the empowered Revenue Court. Because this view conflicted with an earlier Supreme Court decision, the Court referred the matter to a larger Bench.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the definition of tenant in section 2(6) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, read with section 4(5) of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887, and considered sections 8, 9, 14-A and 18 of the 1953 Act and sections 40 and 42 of the 1887 Act. It relied on Bhajan Lal v. State of Punjab, Sanwat Singh v. Zail Singh, Tulsi v. Paro and Ram Lal v. Darshan Lal, and distinguished V. Dhanapal Chettiar v. Yesodai Ammal and R.V. Bhupal Prasad v. State of A.P. as cases concerning rent-control laws. It expressly disagreed with Sukhdev Singh v. Puran, which had treated a fixed-term agricultural tenancy as ending on expiry of the term, and referred the matter to a larger Bench to resolve the conflict.

rule.if: agricultural_tenancy_case and fixed_term_lease_expired and tenant_remained_in_possession and civil_court_possession_claim

predicates.agricultural_tenancy_case: The dispute concerns a person who holds agricultural land under another person as a tenant.
predicates.fixed_term_lease_expired: The agreed fixed term for the tenant’s occupation of the agricultural land came to an end.
predicates.tenant_remained_in_possession: The tenant continued to occupy the agricultural land after the fixed term ended.
predicates.civil_court_possession_claim: The landlord sought possession from the tenant through a civil-court claim.

issues.definition: When a tenant in an agricultural-tenancy dispute remains in possession after a fixed-term lease expires and the landlord seeks possession through a civil-court claim, the tenant is not treated as a trespasser solely because of the expiry and eviction must follow the applicable agricultural-tenancy process.
